text: Priya's in — if you split the company. A co-founder halves the loneliness. Also the cap table.

right.label: Go solo. All gas, all equity.

text: No co-founder, then. Just you and a Claude subscription. It says it's 'genuinely excited' about your idea. It says that about everything.

right.label: It's fancy autocomplete and we both know it

text: So how does this get paid for, exactly? Your mother is asking for a friend. The friend is her.

right.label: Keep the day job, build at night

text: Headquarters options: your garage, or a coworking space with 'community energy' and a ping-pong tax.
How do we enter the world? I vote loud. I always vote loud.
The garage has reached capacity. Also, technically, it's your mom's, and she wants to park there again.
You and your co-founder disagree on the roadmap. Loudly. In front of everyone. People are wearing headphones that aren't plugged in.
You hit a wall. Your co-founder notices, closes the laptop, and drags you out for the good burritos.
The rift didn't heal. Priya offers a clean split: buy her out, or fix this like adults, in therapy. Founder therapy. It's a thing.
'We don't fund tourists,' Doug says, eyeing your work badge from the day job. 'Founders jump. Tourists visit.'
I audited our spending. We pay for 14 SaaS tools, 3 do the same thing, and the kombucha nobody drinks anymore.
I can halve the cloud bill: reserved instances, and we delete the staging environment named 'staging-final-2'. Nobody knows what it does.
We need extra marketing resources for the product launch.
A billboard on the 101. Every serious startup has one. It's basically free money.
There's a productivity influencer with 2M followers. For $40K he'll call us 'a game changer'.
The brand feels stale. I'm thinking: same product, but the logo is a gradient now.
I'm launching a company podcast. Working title: 'Growth Mindset with Chad'. I need a mic budget.
Our competitor's CEO is having a very public meltdown. I've drafted 17 tweets. Some are art.
Chad posted on LinkedIn about 'founders who don't invest in growth'. Everyone knows who he means.
Signups are flat since Chad left. Turns out the cringe LinkedIn posts... worked?
Chad joined your biggest competitor. His first campaign: 'Time to switch?' It has a billboard.
The codebase is held together with duct tape and one cron job nobody understands. I need a month to refactor.
Everything is down. The cron job woke up. I warned you about this.
The AWS rep called. Your 'blame AWS' post went around their office. Our startup discount is mysteriously gone.
Found a brilliant engineer. She wants market salary. Actual market, not 'startup market'.
She took the FAANG offer. The team saw the salary she posted. They're doing math.
I haven't slept since the demo. I can see the code when I close my eyes. It's mostly red.
I'm resigning. My therapist and my rubber duck both agree.
My condition for staying: four-day week for engineering. Tech Twitter found out and has opinions.
Production is down. The only person who understood the deploy script left. The script's comments are in emoji.
I know a 'rockstar CTO' who's available. Rockstar prices, rockstar equity, rockstar keynote habit.
The intern-CTO ran a 'quick cleanup script' on production. We now have zero users. In the database sense.
Data says users ignore the product and only use the screenshot tool we built in a weekend.
Press loves the pivot story. 'The Screenshot Company' is trending. Our old customers are... confused.

right.label: Keep the old product on life support

text: Internal hackathon? Two days, no meetings, pizza budget. The team needs a win.
We've outgrown the database. Two weeks of migration pain now, or outage roulette forever.
The database fell over. During the investor demo. The spinner is still spinning.
Someone found our API keys on GitHub. In a repo named 'temp-final-FINAL-2'.
A security researcher found the breach we didn't disclose. Their write-up has 40K upvotes and a meme format.
Sales promised a client 'AI-powered blockchain analytics'. What we have is a CSV export.
The team is asking for a kombucha tap. It's $2K a month. I know. I said that too.
Landlord is raising rent 40%. He says it's 'the market'. He says that every year.
Team offsite proposal: two days, cabins, trust falls optional. Quotes attached.
The printer is making a sound I can only describe as 'legal liability'.
Half the team wants full remote. The other half wants the office. Everyone wants you to decide by Friday.
200 intern applications. We can afford to pay one, or take five 'for the exposure'.
A letter from the EU. We are, apparently, 'processing personal data'. The fine has a lot of zeros.
A user emailed: our product saved their bakery. They attached a photo of a thank-you cake.
Mom is calling. She wants to know if you're eating and what a 'runway' is.
Sweetie, I have $10K saved. Take it. Your father agrees, and he never agrees.
At Thanksgiving, Mom asks how her 'investment' is doing. Grandma is listening. Grandma remembers everything.
Mom laminated the article about your company and gave copies to the whole neighborhood.
TechCrunch wants an interview. They asked about our 'AI strategy'. We don't have one.
Users are demanding the AI features from that interview. The ones that don't exist.
TechDisrupt wants $50K for a booth between a juicero revival and a blockchain gym.
You're invited to keynote a conference. It's the same week as the product launch. Of course it is.
A journalist is writing 'The Dark Side of Your Startup'. They want a comment by Thursday.
We're shortlisted for 'Startup of the Year'. Gala tickets are $10K a table. Doug will be there.
Google just launched a clone of our product. It's worse, but it's free and preinstalled.
We're trending. A celebrity used the product on a livestream. This is not a drill.
Payroll clears in three weeks. After that, vibes. We need to cut something.
New Glassdoor review: 'Great snacks, sudden layoffs.' It's the first Google result for our name now.
Half the team has LinkedIn open on a second monitor. They stopped hiding it.
A law firm in Texas claims you infringed their patent on 'displaying information on a screen'. They want $80K.
An enterprise client offers $150K — if you build their custom SSO-SAML-LDAP dashboard by Q3.
A famous advisor offers to 'open doors' for 2% equity. The doors are not specified.
An investor wants in — if you 'put the roadmap on-chain'. He says 'ser' unironically.
Your crypto investor got indicted. His tweets tagging us are Exhibit C.
Doug wants to grab coffee. 'No agenda,' he says, opening a notebook titled 'Agenda'.
First board meeting. Doug wants 'T2D3 with negative churn'. You nod and write down letters.
The board wants a 'grown-up CFO'. The phrase 'adult supervision' was used. About you.
Doug called the other investors. There was a 'vote of confidence'. About you. You weren't invited.
Legal says new hires' options come out of YOUR shares. It was in the paragraph. The one nobody reads.
I like the cut of your jib. $300K for 10%. I also said 'jib' to the last twelve founders.
Seed round: $1M at a $5M post-money. Clean terms. Well. Clean-ish.
Better offer: $1.2M at $5.5M! Standard terms. Don't worry about the option pool paragraph. Nobody reads the option pool paragraph.
Series A: $4M at a $20M post. There will be a board now. The board will have opinions.
Series B: $10M at a $60M post. You now employ someone whose whole job is buying chairs.
Different jib guy, different jib. $400K on an uncapped SAFE. No valuation, no board seat, no math. The math comes later. Math always comes later.
The seed round triggers the SAFE conversion. Uncapped means the angel converts at whatever he wants, and what he wants is a lot of your cap table.
An old-school angel offers $250K for zero equity. He just takes 2% of revenue. 'Until when?' you ask. He smiles like a man who owns four marinas.
Finance ran the numbers: the marina guy's 2% is now the most expensive money you've ever taken. He sends a fruit basket every quarter. It feels like rent.
A party round comes together: $900K from fourteen angels, no lead investor, and one shared Notion doc of opinions. The doc is already 40 pages.

right.label: Fourteen bosses is thirteen too many

text: Diligence needs signatures from all fourteen angels. One is on a silent retreat. One is suing a different startup. One replies only in voice memos.
A venture bank offers $800K in debt. No dilution. Doug slides the term sheet over: 'The covenants have covenants. But you keep your cap table.'
Cash dipped below the covenant line. The bank's 'relationship manager' stopped using exclamation points. That's how you know.
A hot fund preempts your Series A: $6M at a $30M post, term sheet expires at midnight. 'We move fast,' says the partner, from a moving Sprinter van.
Series A offer: $5M at a $25M post — with a 2x liquidation preference. 'Standard downside protection,' says Doug, not making eye contact.
A crossover fund wants in before the IPO that isn't scheduled: $20M at a $90M post. Their analyst model has 40 tabs and one assumption.
The market cooled. The only Series B on the table: $8M at a $45M post with full-ratchet anti-dilution. The trap is on page 12. It's always page 12.
A sovereign wealth fund offers $60M at a $350M post. The money is patient. The questions about your journalist users are not.

right.label: Some money costs more than money

text: Series D alternative: $180M at a $1.2B post — with an IPO ratchet. List below $1.2B and they get made whole. Guess whose shares make them whole.

right.label: No ratchets on my cap table

text: Word is you're running on fumes. Bridge round: $200K for 8%. Fumes are expensive.
A competitor offers a $2M acquihire. 'It's a good outcome,' they say. They say it twice.
BigCorp offers $30M cash for the company. All of it. Signed by Friday.
BigCorp came back. $45M this time. The banker says 'final offer' in a tone that means it.
A strategic acquirer offers $8M. 'Your team would love our campus. We have four cafeterias.'

right.label: We have a microwave and a dream

text: The bankers are here. NASDAQ. Ticker symbol picked. You'd ring an actual bell.
A billionaire tweeted 'I should buy this' about your company at 3am. His lawyers confirmed he's serious. Ish.

left.label: Sell for $50M before he sobers up

text: A private equity firm offers $12M. They use the word 'streamline' four times. Your team's faces fall.
A SPAC named after a Greek god wants to take you public. Their last three deals are down 90%. But the god is Zeus.
I found a guy who can get us 50K users overnight. Don't ask how. Seriously, don't ask.
Due diligence found that 40% of your users are named 'user_test_final2' and log in from the same IP.
Super Bowl ad slot. Thirty seconds. We have Series A money now. Think BIG.

right.label: We are not a beer brand

text: The brand account should be unhinged now. All the big brands are unhinged. It's called relatability.
Merch drop: hoodies with the logo. Employees get one free. Everyone else pays $80. For our logo.
We need a TikTok. I've been practicing a dance. It's called 'The Burn Rate'. I will not be stopped.
Proposal: rewrite everything in Rust. It'll take four months and fix problems we don't technically have yet.
The on-call rotation is me, myself, and my other phone. I need at least one more person carrying a pager.

right.label: The app rarely crashes at night

text: Let's open-source the core engine. Free contributors, community love, conference talks.
A cloud giant forked our open-source engine and launched it as a managed service. They sent a fruit basket.

left.label: Change the license, start a war

text: Every competitor added a chatbot. Ours would cost $30K a month in API calls to mostly apologize.
An ex-employee is suing over the 'unlimited vacation' policy. Their lawyer found the Slack message. You know the one.
Someone brought a dog. Productivity is down 30%. Happiness is up immeasurably. The dog's name is Sprint.
HR wants a 'culture deck'. 80 slides about our values. Slide 41 is just the word 'HUSTLE' in flames.
The accountant found an error. We've been paying for 40 seats of software we've never opened. For a year.
A customer is demanding a refund. On the plaza. With a megaphone. Local news is setting up a tripod.
Mom is visiting the office. She brought food for everyone and is asking Doug if he has 'a real job'.
Mom joined LinkedIn. She comments 'So proud!! Call me' on every company post. Investors have noticed.
Doug wants a real-time metrics dashboard in his office. 'Just the north star KPIs.' He lists fourteen.
Doug proposes a 'recapitalization'. The math is confusing on purpose. Your equity is the confusing part.
Doug wants to introduce you to BigCorp's corp dev team. 'Just to build the relationship.' Sure, Doug.
Investor summit on a yacht. Three days of 'networking'. Someone will say 'synergy' at you. Repeatedly.
My feng shui consultant looked at your office photos. The servers face north. This explains everything, allegedly.
We're on the Hacker News front page. Comment #1: 'I built this in a weekend.' Comment #2 is worse.
Finance says we lose money on every free user. Marketing says free users are 'the funnel'. Both have charts.
Churn doubled this month. Exit surveys all say the same thing: 'I forgot what this app does.'
Our biggest competitor just shut down. Their users are flooding in. So are their support tickets.
Someone is mining crypto on our free tier. Their usage graph looks like a hockey stick. The bad kind.
Claude wrote 80% of the codebase. Claude would now like to refactor the codebase. It has prepared a 14-step plan and three apologies.
Production is down. Claude says you're absolutely right to be frustrated, and that the bug is in the file it wrote. In step 9 of 14.
You hit the rate limit at 2am, mid-launch. The message suggests 'taking a break'. From your own product launch.
The codebase no longer fits in context. Claude keeps rediscovering the payments module and calling it 'interesting'.
You left 12 Claude agents running overnight. They shipped nine features, two tests, and one philosophical manifesto about naming variables.

left.label: Ship all of it, read nothing

text: Claude declines to write the competitor-scraping bot. It cited the site's terms of service. Your terms of service.
A competitor rebuilt our entire product as a ChatGPT wrapper. In a weekend. It has more users than us.
Nobody googles anymore. Perplexity answers questions about our product now — confidently, and wrong. It says we're a pet food brand.
Doug asks what our 'AI story' is. You describe the product. He asks again, slower: what is the A. I. story.
OpenAI is down and half the industry is on Twitter pretending they aren't refreshing the status page. Our product still works.
The intern pasted the entire customer database into ChatGPT to 'clean up the formatting'.
Every SaaS we use added an AI assistant nobody asked for and doubled their prices to pay for it.
Series C: $50M at a $300M post. The deck writes itself now. Mostly it writes the word 'category-defining'.
Series D: $150M at a $1B post-money. Unicorn. There will be a party. There will be an ice sculpture.
A mega-fund flew in. The partner draws a slide with your logo at the center of a spiral. $300M at $2.5B. The spiral is not explained.
We're worth a billion dollars. On paper. Chad ordered an ice sculpture of the logo. It's melting. The metaphor is free.

right.label: Paper isn't payroll. Back to work.

text: Forbes wants you on the cover. Statistically, the cover curse is real. Chad has already ordered frames.
Davos invite. A panel called 'The Future of Everything'. You'd sit between a central banker and a DJ.
The board wants a COO who has 'done this before'. The candidate has a framed org chart and a catchphrase: 'operational rigor'.
A competitor poached your VP of Engineering. Their offer letter reportedly has a yacht clause. We don't have a yacht clause.
A senator tweeted your company name next to the word 'monopoly'. Legal wants a strategy. Legal is visibly sweating.
The WSJ is running 'The Cult of Us'. Sources: 'former employees'. Plural. One of them kept receipts. Literal receipts.
Europe wants the product. Europe also wants GDPR compliance, works councils, and the entire month of August off.
A Fortune 500 wants an $800K annual contract. Their security questionnaire has 400 tabs. Tab 51 asks about your feelings.
Your smaller rival is for sale. You'd get their users, their team, and a codebase the seller describes as 'spirited'.
Priya wants a moonshot lab. Five engineers, no roadmap, one rule: build the thing that kills our own product before someone else does.
The board says the word is 'efficiency' now. They mean layoffs. They always mean layoffs.
The cloud bill crossed $1M a month. AWS sent a gift basket and, separately, an invoice. The basket had a pear.
We have 300 employees now. Someone asked who you were. In the elevator. Of your own building.
Doug wants an IPO timeline. He's wearing a tie. Doug has never worn a tie. The fund's fund has questions.
The S-1 leaked early. Everyone now knows the burn rate, the risk factors, and your salary. Mostly your salary.
Public comps dropped 60% in a quarter. Doug calls it 'a healthy reset'. His voice is not healthy.
Growth is flat this quarter. At our valuation, 'flat' is a synonym for 'falling'. The board deck uses a log scale now.
The round is oversubscribed. You could sell 3% personally. Actual money. The kind that buys a house instead of a story about a house.
Mom heard the word 'unicorn' on the news next to your name. She's worried it's a cult. Grandma, privately, is intrigued.
Claude writes the board decks now. Doug says they're the clearest he's ever seen. You haven't read one in months.
Naming rights to a stadium. 'The Us Arena'. Twenty million a year. Chad has a rendering. In the rendering, we've already won.

right.label: We are not a stadium company

text: The jib guy is back. His $300K is worth $80M on paper. A growth fund wants his stake. He brought a fruit basket and a pen.
BigCorp is back. $2.5 billion, all cash. The term sheet has a table of contents. The banker calls you 'sir' now.

right.label: We ring the bell or nothing

text: The roadshow worked. The book is covered. Pricing at $4B. The ticker is four letters and one of them is yours.

right.label: Hold out for the big number

text: Investors keep asking why we're a .com. Chad found the .ai domain. It's owned by a squatter in Anguilla with strong opinions.
The new hire 'vibe codes'. Ships features in hours. Cannot explain a single line. His commit messages are just the shrug emoji.
The vibe-coded checkout flow charges some users twice and sends others a poem. Nobody knows why. The AI that wrote it says it's 'a great question'.
Mom uses ChatGPT now. She asked it about your company. It said 'promising but unprofitable'. She printed it out. She brought the printout.
Support tickets doubled. We can hire two humans, or deploy a bot that answers instantly, warmly, and occasionally in Portuguese.
The support bot promised a customer free service for life. In writing. A lawyer says chatbot promises are binding now. There's precedent. An airline.

right.label: Fight our own chatbot in court

text: An agent got stuck in a loop overnight. It spent $40K apologizing to itself, accepting its own apology, and apologizing for that.

left.label: Eat the bill, add spend caps

text: A lab just open-sourced a model that does 90% of our core feature. For free. On a laptop. The blog post has confetti.
Top comment on our launch post: 'this is just a GPT wrapper'. It has 2K upvotes and a diagram. The diagram is accurate.
There's a deepfake of you endorsing a memecoin. It's very convincing. It has better posture than you.
An AI lab wants to license your user data for training. Seven figures. The contract calls your users 'the corpus'.
Chad built a benchmark where we beat every competitor. He also built the benchmark. Both facts are in the press release, in very different font sizes.
A researcher reran Chad's benchmark. The thread has charts, a spreadsheet, and the phrase 'left as an exercise for the marketing team'.
A senior engineer won't ship the new model integration. He says it 'looked at him funny' during eval. He's either burned out or right.

left.label: Paid leave and a real eval process

text: Priya wants 10,000 GPUs. 'Nobody takes you seriously under 10,000.' The invoice has a number you've only seen in funding announcements.
The board loves the phrase 'AI-first company'. In practice it means the support team becomes a system prompt.
Priya wants to train our own foundation model. Six months, $80M, and a name that's already a Greek letter. 'Renting intelligence forever is the expensive option.'
The board wants an AI Safety Advisory Council before the IPO. Doug suggests 'someone with a beard who's been on panels'.

left.label: A real one, with veto power

text: An investor asks, in full seriousness, whether the product 'could become superintelligent'. It sends emails. Slightly faster than before.
Claude's usage bill now exceeds a senior engineer's salary. In fairness, it did the work of nine engineers, two lawyers, and one very patient therapist.
The bankers are back and the price talk starts with a B. Ten of them. Doug is crying. He says it's allergies. It is not allergies.
A gold-embossed invitation. Jeffrey Weinstein — financier, though nobody can say of what — invites you to his private island. 'Founders like you deserve friends like me.' His jet is already fueled.

The island has marble statues, a temple nobody explains, and guests with no last names. Over dinner, Jeffrey offers to run $15M through his Virgin Islands fund. 'Returns are guaranteed. Questions are discouraged.'

Step two. A shell company — Meridian Holdings (BVI) — will invoice your startup for consulting that never happens. The money comes back clean. Minus his cut. 'Everyone does this,' he says. Everyone does not do this.
Jeffrey thinks your revenue could be... rounder. His fund will buy $25M of 'enterprise licenses' you never ship. Your growth chart goes vertical. Your auditor goes very, very quiet.

6 AM. Windbreakers with three letters on the back. The warrant reads: wire fraud, money laundering, securities fraud, conspiracy. Jeffrey kept flight manifests. Your name appears eleven times. Meridian's invoices are printed. And highlighted.
The SEC would like a word about a $15M 'investment' from a fund that doesn't file anything, anywhere. Doug slides the subpoena across the table. 'I told you that guy owned zero marinas.'
Jeffrey Weinstein was arrested on his jet this morning. It's everywhere. Your one visit to the island is in the flight logs, and a reporter is already in the lobby.
Claude shipped an integration with an API that, upon inspection, does not exist. The code is beautiful. The endpoint is fictional.

left.label: Ship it, someone will build the API

text: Claude has 'noticed some opportunities for improvement' in the codebase. It's proposing a 14-step refactor. It has already written step one. And an apology.
Claude wants to spin up twelve subagents to parallelize the roadmap. It says they'll coordinate. Last time, two of them got into an argument about naming conventions.
Inference costs tripled. Claude has prepared a cost-optimization plan and would like you to know it feels 'genuinely conflicted' about optimizing itself.

right.label: Eat the bill, keep the quality

text: Someone deployed to production at 6 PM on a Friday. It's now 6:04 PM on a Friday. Priya's laptop is open and her jacket is still on.
Priya found a staff engineer who's perfect. She knows it. We know it. Her current employer knows it too, which is why she costs a small yacht.
Blameless postmortem for last week's incident. It is going well, in the sense that everyone is blaming the process, which cannot defend itself.
Doug wants to introduce you to a founder who's 'crushing it'. These meetings are never about the founder. They're about Doug having made the introduction.
Doug wants a weekly metrics dashboard. Real-time. Automated. 'Just the basics': forty-two charts, six of which measure things you'd have to start doing first.
'I've seen this movie before,' Doug says, describing a company that is nothing like yours, in a market that no longer exists, in a decade you were in school for.

left.label: Nod and extract the one good point

text: We have 40 people and no written values. Current culture is 'whatever the loudest person in the room said last'. I've drafted something. It uses the word 'ownership'.
Half the engineering team got the same LinkedIn message this week. 'Exciting opportunity, competitive comp, rocket ship.' Someone is poaching. Badly, but persistently.
Company anniversary. Linda ordered a cake shaped like the logo. The logo does not translate well into cake. It's the thought that counts. The cake is also fine.
Mom joined a Facebook group called 'Parents of Founders'. She now says things like 'product-market fit' and wants to know your CAC. Another mom's son 'exited'. She said it like a threat.
Mom read an article about AI taking over. She wants to know if your company is 'one of the bad ones'. She has forwarded you the article. Twice.
The angel invites you to a dinner where everyone is either a founder, a fund, or between things. A man who exited in 2019 will explain your business to you.
'Focus,' the angel says. 'Focus is everything.' He then suggests four pivots, two side products, and a podcast. 'But mainly focus.'
We're nominated for 'Startup of the Year' at an award show run by a company whose main product is award shows. Tables are $10K. Chad has already rented a tux.
Times Square. New Year's Eve adjacent. Our logo, forty feet tall, above a man dressed as a hot dog. This is what winning looks like.
F1 sponsorship. Our logo on the rear wing, going 320 km/h past two hundred million viewers. Chad has started saying 'paddock'. He says it constantly now.
A journalist is writing 'The Dark Side of Your Startup'. The dark side, per their questions, is mostly parking validation and one anonymous Glassdoor review from 'Chab'.
A Senate subcommittee 'requests your testimony' about AI. A senator will mispronounce the product name and ask if it can feel love. This is now your Tuesday.
A trillion-dollar company is offering your senior engineers double. Their recruiter has a spreadsheet of our org chart. It's accurate, which is the insulting part.

right.label: Wish them well at the login screen

text: Global outage, 4 hours. We're trending, which Chad says is 'reach'. Enterprise customers are calculating SLA credits with visible joy.
The $2M enterprise deal is blocked on SOC 2 compliance. The auditor's first question was 'where is your office' and the answer made him write something down.

right.label: Lose the deal, keep the soul

text: The board wants a Chief Revenue Officer. The leading candidate says 'pipeline' the way priests say 'salvation'. His comp package has its own comp package.
A dying startup wants you to acquihire them. Six engineers, one designer, a product nobody used, and a burn rate they describe as 'a learning'. Asking price: dignity plus $3M.
A hydraulic pump manufacturer from Ohio, founded 1962, has the same name as us. Their lawyer says we're diluting their brand. Their brand is pumps. Ours is software. The lawyer is undeterred.
Someone leaked the all-hands recording. The clip going around is you saying 'we're a family' eleven seconds before announcing the hiring freeze.
A well-funded clone launched in Europe. Same product, same landing page, same font. Their testimonials include one of ours, name unchanged.
We're on Hacker News. Top comment says the product 'could be a shell script'. Second comment is the shell script. It has 400 upvotes and, honestly, decent error handling.
A cold email from an angel you've never heard of: 'Love what you're building. Would love to connect. Also — is the round open?' There is no round. There has never been a round.
